d_sv_content.name: Evaluating whole abdomen radiation therapy as a treatment for feline small cell gastrointestinal lymphoma
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us determine if whole abdomen radiation therapy helps cats with small cell gastrointestinal lymphoma
d_sv_content.description: This study will evaluate how well-tolerated whole abdomen radiation is for cats diagnosed with small cell lymphoma. The goal of this study is to establish a safe and practical radiation protocol and to monitor treatment response in cats with gastrointestinal small cell lymphoma (i.e., cancer involving the stomach or intestines).
d_sv_content.requirements: Day 0: Patients will have an oncology exam, blood collection, and urine collection. Prior to this first appointment, owners will be asked to collect a fresh fecal sample from their pet at home to bring with them to this appointment. Radiation therapy under general anesthesia will also be started.Days 1 through 4: Each day, for a total of four days, cats will be placed under general anesthesia for approximately 20-30 minutes while radiation therapy is administered. Once they are awake and recovered from anesthesia, cats can be discharged to go home with their owners unless an overnight stay is indicated.2 weeks and 6 weeks post radiation therapy: Just like Day 0, cats will have an oncology exam, blood collection, and urine collection. Owners should bring a fresh sample of their cat’s feces to these appointments.
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Pet owners are responsible for bringing their cat on time to each scheduled appointment. Owners will need to collect a fecal sample from their cat at home to bring to the Day 0 visit as well as the 2 and 6 weeks post therapy follow up visits. There will be a quality of life survey for owners to fill out electronically at each visit and every 2 months for up to 18 months (~ 1-2 min time commitment).
d_sv_content.whoCan: We are looking to enroll:Cats with gastrointestinal small cell lymphoma confirmed with biopsy that are newly diagnosed but challenging to medicate or those that have relapsed (failed previous chemotherapy) will be eligible for enrollment. Within 14 days of enrollment, analysis of blood and urine will be needed to determine general health for treatment and anesthesia. Cats cannot have been given any chemotherapy or corticosteroids for at least 7 days before radiation therapy begins. Clients must live within a 6 hour drive from College Station Texas.
d_sv_content.benefits: There are risks associated with general anesthesia and the radiation therapy treatment. These risks will be discussed with each owner before any cat is enrolled.
d_sv_content.compensation:
Owners are responsible for the costs associated with the blood and urine panels performed about14 days before enrollment to determine enrollment eligibility. 

Once enrolled in the study, all study-related costs are covered. If a cat needs to be housed overnight, there may be costs associated with housing in our hospital.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment:
There are a total of 7 visits associated with this study. Days 0 and 1-4 will be day long appointments where radiation therapy is given under general anesthesia. In some instances, patients may stay overnight.

2 weeks and 6 weeks later, each visit can last anywhere from 2-4 hours.
